chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked him about a man who comes to al-Masjid al-Haram and has resolved to perform Hajj, and he performs Tawaf around the House. He said: 'Yes, as long as he has not entered into Ihram.'
ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim perform Tawaf before entering Ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam clarifies that a pilgrim may perform Tawaf al-Qudum (arrival circumambulation) before assuming the state of Ihram, provided the formal intention (niyyah) and ritual consecration have not yet occurred. This ruling highlights the flexibility in the sequence of Hajj rituals, distinguishing between the physical act of circumambulation and the legal status of being in Ihram, a key distinction in Shia fiqh for those arriving by land or sea.
